title: Cross-functional launch playbook for SDKs: structured output + streaming with examples and coordinated release notes
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Coordinate launch activities across Product, Engineering, Design, Docs, SDKs, and Marketing for the new structured output and streaming API surface. Deliver language-specific examples, a canonical set of release notes, an internal support runbook, and measurable GTM artifacts. Ensure all artifacts are reviewer-approved and ready for the release window.
goals: 1) Ship consistent SDK examples (Python, TypeScript, Go, Java) demonstrating function-calling + structured output and streaming. 2) Create a single-source release notes doc that PRs into product website and SDK changelogs. 3) Align Console/Telemetry + Support with new fields and breaking changes. 4) Publish GTM materials (announcement draft, sample apps, blog outline).
success_metrics: 1) Examples merged in SDK repos and live in docs by due_date. 2) Release notes approved by PM+Engineering+Legal. 3) <2 support tickets in first 72 hours, median time-to-first-response < 1 hour. 4) 10+ demo signups from initial announcement week.
tasks: Finalize API changelog entry and public examples matrix
Create language-specific example implementations for function-calling + structured output + streaming (Python, TS, Go, Java)
Author canonical release notes and changelog snippets for SDK repos
Coordinate design review for sample app screenshots and code snippets
Integrate telemetry events and console surface notes (Console team)
Prepare support runbook and triage flow; include sample logs and common errors
Draft marketing announcement, blog outline, and demo scripts
Create SDK migration notes and backward-compatibility section
Schedule cross-team launch readiness review and sign-off meeting
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): docs + SDK PRs merged behind feature flag; invite 5 early customers. Phase 2 (public docs + SDK stable releases): swap feature flag, publish release notes, blog post, and examples. Phase 3 (observable + metrics): monitor telemetry and rollback policy for first 48 hours. Use canary routing for high-traffic models if instability detected.
release_notes_draft: Highlights: Structured output now supports typed JSON schema and explicit field validation; streaming responses available with incremental events and final completion markers; function-calling behavior refined for nested objects. Breaking changes: default structured output strictness raised (opt-out via strict=false). Upgrade notes: SDK vX.Y.Z adds new streaming client and structured-output helper utilities. See code snippets in Examples section.
sample_matrix: We will produce a canonical matrix that maps feature -> languages -> example filenames: structured-output/simple-json.py, structured-output/streaming-chat.ts, function-calls/order_flow.go, function-calls/receipt-java. Each example must have runnable README, tests, and CI steps. Samples should be small (<= 80 LOC) and demonstrate error handling, schema validation, and streaming partial results.
support_runbook: Include triage checklist, relevant logs/console traces, mapping from error codes to user-facing guidance, escalation path to Engineering on-call, and sample quick-fix PRs for common issues. Owner: Claire Huang. Publish as internal doc and attach to the release notes internal page.
comms_plan: Pre-announce to partners and select customers during internal beta. Day-of: blog + product changelog + SDK release notes + code samples. Week following: technical webinar and short walkthrough videos. Marketing to run a targeted email to existing dev accounts and tweet thread highlighting developer ergonomics.
post_launch_monitoring: Primary signals: SDK install/upgrade errors, docs pageviews, support tickets, API error-rate on structured-output endpoints, latency for streaming sessions. Thresholds: error-rate spike > 0.5% roll back or open hotfix. Weekly metric review for first 4 weeks.
open_questions: Should we include a migration script for customers using legacy structured output?
Do we need a compatibility shim in SDKs for strict=false default?
Legal sign-off needed for marketing claim language around latency improvements?
launch_checklist: All SDK PRs merged and released (tags created)
Docs live and example code runnable in CI
Release notes published in product changelog and SDK repos
Support runbook published and support team trained
Final cross-team launch review completed and signed off
